messages:
eval-bot: Nightly eval finished for cohort=product_faqs. Regression detected:
- recall@10: 0.78 -> 0.68 (-12.8%)
- NDCG@5: 0.81 -> 0.64 (-20.9%)
Signal: reranker v2.1.3 (deployed canary 1718420000).
Full report: https://ci.internal/reports/nightly/1718501234

anya: who rolled v2.1.3 to canary? noted the timing matches the drop.

james: that was me, rolled after PR #432 merged. small training change: increased margin weight and switched to in-batch hard negatives.

li: dropping the PR diff here: ```diff
- loss = 0.9 * ce + 0.1 * margin
+ loss = 0.7 * ce + 0.3 * margin
// also enabled hard_negatives=True```

sofia: quick repro summary (ran local eval against canary endpoints):
- ANN only (embedder q8): recall@10 ~0.77 -> 0.75 (minor)
- full pipeline (ann -> reranker v2.1.3): recall@10 0.78 -> 0.68, NDCG@5 0.81 -> 0.64
Conclusion: reranker behavior change, not embedding drift.

mike: can you paste example queries where reranker over-ranked bad docs? would help narrow loss change effects.

sofia: example: query "How do I reset API key?"
- top doc (old): KB article "Resetting keys (step-by-step)" (relevance 0.98)
- top doc (v2.1.3): forum thread with unrelated config discussion (relevance 0.22)

james: interesting — the new hard negatives may have pushed the reranker away from surface-level lexical matches toward recall of paraphrases, which hurts short queries with exact-match targets. I prioritized harder negatives to reduce hallucination but maybe overshot.

anya: two immediate actions: 1) pin canary to v2.1.2 while we triage; 2) run targeted eval comparing v2.1.2 vs v2.1.3 on short-query cohorts + long-query cohorts to see impact surface.

james: opening rollback PR now: #438 — rolling back to v2.1.2 weights and disabling hard_negatives for a quick canary revert. ETA deploy 20m.

li: running retro eval job: `python eval/run_rag_eval.py --cohort product_faqs --rerankers v2.1.2,v2.1.3 --embedder q8 --out /tmp/triage/171850` (approx 45m). will post summarized diffs.

sofia: also adding a small prompt set of 150 short, exact-match queries to our regression suite. if v2.1.3 still wins on longform but fails shortform, we can try hybrid policy: route short queries to v2.1.2.

mike: flagging eng-oncall in case rollback affects traffic: @eng-oncall please watch canary rollback.

anya: one more thing — capture reranker confidence distribution (score hist) pre/post. that will show whether margin upweighting is compressing scores. james can you add logging hook to canary?

james: yep adding hist logging to /metrics/reranker/score_histogram and will push a 2-min aggregation.

eval-bot: Quick follow-up: ad-hoc test (sofia) diff output: 
- short-query recall@1: 0.92 -> 0.71
- long-query recall@10: 0.66 -> 0.68
So regression concentrated in short queries.

anya: good catch. plan: revert canary now, run overnight eval with new short-query suite, then schedule a controlled retrain with tuned margin/hard-negative ratio. assign owners: james (rollback & retrain followup), li (diagnostics + eval), sofia (regression suite & examples).

sofia: noted. adding example cases to the bug report and uploading sample contexts.

james: rollback deployed to canary at 1718501430. monitoring metrics.

mike: saw canary metrics return to baseline within ~3 minutes. :thumbsup:

li: retro eval job finished (summary): overall ndcg diff narrowed to -2% after rollback on short suite. full report: https://ci.internal/reports/nightly/1718501234/triage

anya: great. leaving this thread open until the controlled retrain is scheduled. thanks all. :heart:
